claims.statement: Prefer Sarween Tools and Plasma Scoring as the usual starting technologies; the speakers strongly reject Neural Motivator as a default.
claims.conditions: Their default path; a table-specific choice to deny another faction Sarween is acknowledged but not recommended.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Strong podcast preference; not universal advice.

claims.statement: Treat the home system as influence-rich but awkward for early resources and production.
claims.conditions: This matters when planning the opening economy and weighing Hololattice against another dock.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Values and strategic impact are guide claims; verify exact planet values against the rules source.

claims.statement: Use Zeal’s player-count-scaled early votes as leverage, while recognizing that voting first can be a liability.
claims.conditions: Its bonus applies if Argent casts a vote; the hosts are especially negative about three- or four-player games.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Agenda outcomes depend on table agreements and player count.

claims.statement: Use the starting Strike Wing Alpha I destroyers as cheap two-move capacity units, not as ordinary destroyers.
claims.conditions: They can carry a small invasion force, reach custodians, and threaten distant systems alongside the starting carrier.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Cheap reach is the point; the guide does not claim late-game durability.

claims.statement: Exploit Aerie Sentinels’ capacity-free transport to make unexpected or flexible landings.
claims.conditions: A capacity ship must be present; the guide says any number of Argent mechs can accompany it without counting against capacity.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Mechanic is summarized from the episode, not separately rules-checked.

claims.statement: Use Trilossa Aun Mirik to spread home-produced ground forces across Argent’s three-planet home system.
claims.conditions: Most useful on a large home production; the guide describes the agent as convenient but modest otherwise.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Ability application follows the podcast explanation.

claims.statement: Unlock Trrakan Aun Zulok early by building toward six units with AFB, space cannon, or bombardment.
claims.conditions: The starting destroyers and home PDS make the unlock accessible; one example is taking Construction secondary and building two destroyers at home.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Threshold and ability are transcript descriptions, not a separate rules ruling.

claims.statement: Remember that the commander adds a die to one unit-ability roll, including anti-fighter barrage.
claims.conditions: The guide names AFB, space cannon, and bombardment; it warns digital tabletop users not to forget to enable the extra die.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Mod implementation may vary.

claims.statement: Treat Mirik Aun Sissiri as an opportunistic defensive or repositioning tool, not the foundation of a strategy.
claims.conditions: Her action moves ships between tokened systems with no enemy ships; the guide values late defense, with invasion or Malice access as situational cases.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts differ slightly on clever use frequency; both call it situational.

claims.statement: The episode’s FAQ interpretation allows transport out of tokened systems during a movement ability; keep that distinct from a tactical action.
claims.conditions: Relevant to the Argent hero and comparable movement abilities.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: FAQ/errata version is date-sensitive; verify before rules adjudication.

claims.statement: Prioritize Strike Wing Alpha II; treat its 9-or-10 infantry effect as extra rather than the main benefit.
claims.conditions: A core upgrade for a faction encouraged to build destroyers; infantry aboard ships are the threat described.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The infantry-kill FAQ is episode-specific and unverified here.

claims.statement: Research Aerie Hololattice when production or a home-system fix matters; do not assume its movement restriction secures every slice.
claims.conditions: Its Production 1 is attractive at home and on forward planets; the defensive value depends on slice geometry and opponent routes.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The guide calls it slice-dependent and says opponents can work around it.

claims.statement: The preferred core technology package is PDS II plus Strike Wing Alpha II.
claims.conditions: PDS II deters bullying while Strike Wing II provides efficient midgame fleets; exact timing depends on the board.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: “Almost every game” is the speakers’ preference, not a requirement.

claims.statement: Consider AI Development Algorithm as an early rebate that bridges core research into a late-game unit upgrade.
claims.conditions: One proposed path is PDS II, AI Dev, then Strike Wing II; DET or Antimass may fill prerequisites for Carrier II or Dreadnought II.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is one suggested no-skip path, not the only route; confirm current prerequisites.

claims.statement: Choose Carrier II or Dreadnought II according to production and the fleet role needed.
claims.conditions: The hosts lean Dread II when production is limited, Carrier II when extra infantry/capacity is needed; Dread II adds bombardment opportunities.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Contextual preference; objectives, fleet and resources change the choice.

claims.statement: Use Dark Energy Tap selectively with Argent’s destroyer-heavy fleet, which can explore and later reposition.
claims.conditions: The destroyers remain useful for home defense or late offense, making DET more plausible than for factions using disposable explorers.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Exploration rewards and tech tempo determine value; not automatic.

claims.statement: Reserve Graviton Laser Systems for late-game defense; research earlier only for a visible threat.
claims.conditions: The hosts allow earlier Graviton if Argent took custodians, the table has noticed, and Carrier II is not urgent.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Highly table-dependent advice.

claims.statement: Use Fleet Logistics to make a planned hero reposition harder to block, not as a token-only feint.
claims.conditions: The value is in staging ships, taking a planet, then using the hero to return or defend before opponents can obstruct the destination.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Situational combo; not a general requirement.

claims.statement: Treat Assault Cannon as an optional red-skip finisher for small ships, not a blind default.
claims.conditions: The proposed combination uses AFB and Raid Formation before combat; the speakers recommend it only when a concrete target makes sense.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Conditional tech opinion; access and target matter.

claims.statement: Do not make Integrated Economy or Self-Assembly Routines routine investments; cheap destroyer-plus-mech production already covers much of the role.
claims.conditions: A fitting skip or unusual objective can change the choice, but usual tech tempo and available build sites make them hard to justify.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts’ judgment reflects their typical games, not every map.

claims.statement: Sell Strike Wing Ambuscade near its ability window; do not overprice vague passive defense, but ask more when it directly enables scoring.
claims.conditions: The extra die matters most for a planned offensive/objective roll; Jol-Nar is a stronger buyer because of rerolls.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Negotiation value depends on the scoring window.

claims.statement: Use the PDS network as a paid deterrent; establish a simple consistent toll and avoid giving space-cannon value away for nothing.
claims.conditions: The speakers suggest roughly one trade good normally, with negotiation when the passage or objective is especially important.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: A table heuristic, not a market rule; route alternatives matter.

claims.statement: Keep trade simple and frequent: Argent has three commodities but often reaches more neighbors early than its commodity value suggests.
claims.conditions: Several small trades and X-1 opportunities are preferred to one elaborate exchange; Trade can fund flexible spending.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); compatibility with current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Depends on neighbors, map and table norms.

claims.statement: Choose round-one cards by whether they enable custodians timing, not a fixed ranking.
claims.conditions: Trade, Warfare, or a timed Diplomacy/Technology/Leadership combination may work depending on skips, secondaries, and table choices.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts differ on rankings; they agree to assess actual variables.

claims.statement: Take Politics when speaker position can preserve round-two custodians or help later speaker control.
claims.conditions: Less attractive if round-one custodians is available another way; assess whether the next speaker can score early.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts differ on later speaker value.

claims.statement: If custodians is unavailable and Construction is a late pick, place a forward PDS on an important equidistant or in-slice planet.
claims.conditions: The hosts favor a forward PDS on valuable slice planets; placement depends on map geometry and neighbors.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Map geometry and neighbors determine placement.

claims.statement: Do not prioritize Leadership automatically; take it when token pressure or a blue-skip Gravity Drive opening makes its timing valuable.
claims.conditions: Home influence often funds one extra token; Leadership is more attractive if it enables round-one Gravity Drive and a later Mecatol grab.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Map and resource situation matter.

claims.statement: Start planning the late fleet by round three: Strike Wing IIs can lose when opponents bring more sustained hull points.
claims.conditions: Build toward fleet-pool advantage; add carriers, fighters, or dreadnoughts according to objectives, with Hololattice as possible forward production.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: No fixed fleet recipe.

claims.statement: Argent is well positioned for many stage-one control and economic objectives, but early comfort should not obscure custodians’ bonus-point value.
claims.conditions: Movement and capacity help with early control; inexpensive fleets and modest tech needs soften stage-one spending objectives.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Map and objective order matter; printed scoring conditions still apply.

claims.statement: Expect weaker stage-two economic scoring and prepare an upgraded fleet for major control objectives.
claims.conditions: Structure objectives may suit Argent; large resource reserves and taking defended planets can be difficult without ship upgrades.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Guide forecast depends on objective, map, opponents and prior investment.

claims.statement: Use bonus AFB rolls to pursue combat secrets such as Turn Their Fleets to Dust and Fight with Precision; treat Occupy the Fringe and Produce en Masse as awkward fits.
claims.conditions: Demonstrate Your Power is described as broadly accessible rather than a distinct Argent advantage; printed scoring conditions still apply.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts correct their own mix-up between Demonstrate Your Power and Make an Example in the discussion.

claims.statement: Watch for Representative Government, Articles of War, Rearmament Agreement, and Enforced Travel Ban.
claims.conditions: They can remove Zeal’s bonus votes, suppress the mech, or disable PDS near wormholes; allies and agenda control may help.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Agenda text and FAQ state may be date-sensitive; verify before acting.

claims.statement: After missing custodians, pursue an attainable bonus-point route, but avoid resource-intensive exploration gambles without the means to support them.
claims.conditions: One host suggests DET or an accessible Mecatol point route; the other argues Argent lacks Naaz-Rokha’s wealth and repeatable exploration tempo.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers explicitly disagree; the best route depends on the game.

claims.statement: Use PDS placement and Hololattice to defend valuable routes and production sites, allowing for exposed approaches in an awkward slice.
claims.conditions: Structures on tech skips or attachment planets can deter attacks; empty systems and wormhole geometry can undermine coverage.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Defense is a deterrent; the guide says slice layout matters.

claims.statement: Do not let early control scores or defense justify delaying the point plan.
claims.conditions: Without custodians or another bonus point, Argent may struggle once stage twos arrive; round-three decisions often determine its tempo.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 289 (2023-03-08); current-rules compatibility unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is the hosts’ play experience, not a guaranteed outcome.

connections.conditions: Sarween is the normal yellow start; Hololattice Production 1 receives its production discount.
When both modifiers apply to a qualifying ability roll, the guide describes an especially threatening home PDS roll.
Together they provide the guide’s preferred deterrence and low-cost midgame fleet package; neither guarantees safety.
Fleet Logistics can stage the fleet before hero movement, reducing the chance an opponent blocks an empty destination.
The guide says the proposed Jol-Nar alliance exchange makes Argent’s PDS network much stronger, while describing it as a political tradeoff.
